structures.name: C0–C1 atlanto-occipital joint
structures.source: Dreyfuss, Michaelsen & Fletcher, Spine 1994 — provocative intra-articular injection, 5 asymptomatic volunteers.
structures.note: Consistently suboccipital; may extend cephalad toward the vertex and occasionally the frontal region. Very small volunteer sample (N=5) — treat the zone as indicative, not precise.

structures.name: C1–C2 lateral atlanto-axial joint
structures.source: Dreyfuss et al., Spine 1994 (N=5 volunteers); clinical validation by controlled blocks — Aprill, Axinn & Bogduk, Cephalalgia 2002 (21/34 patients confirmed).
structures.note: Discrete unilateral pain at the occipito-cervical junction, retromastoid area and upper cervical region. Aprill's clinical criteria (occipital pain + focal C1 transverse process tenderness + restricted rotation) had only 60% positive predictive value — distribution alone cannot substitute for a diagnostic block.

structures.name: C2–C3 facet joint (third occipital nerve)
structures.source: Dwyer, Aprill & Bogduk, Spine 1990 — volunteer distension; validated clinically in Aprill et al. 1990; Lord et al., JNNP 1994 — controlled double-blind blocks.
structures.note: Upper neck pain extending into the head — toward the ear, vertex, forehead or eye. The most common source of headache after whiplash: third occipital nerve headache found in 27% of whiplash patients overall and 53% of those whose dominant complaint was headache.
structures.lookalikes: Cervicogenic headache from C1–2; occipital neuralgia; migraine

structures.name: C3–C4 facet joint
structures.source: Dwyer, Aprill & Bogduk, Spine 1990 — volunteer distension; corroborated in symptomatic patients by Fukui et al., Pain 1996.
structures.note: Neck pain from the suboccipital region down to the lower neck — characteristically WITHOUT shoulder involvement. That absence is the useful discriminator from C4–5 and below.

structures.name: C4–C5 facet joint
structures.source: Dwyer, Aprill & Bogduk, Spine 1990 — volunteer distension; Fukui et al., Pain 1996.
structures.note: More caudally located than C3–4: top of the shoulder and the lower part of the neck. Fukui found lower posterior cervical in 76% and suprascapular in 43% of symptomatic patients.

structures.name: C5–C6 facet joint
structures.source: Dwyer, Aprill & Bogduk, Spine 1990 — volunteer distension; Fukui et al., Pain 1996; prevalence data from Cooper, Bailey & Bogduk, Pain Medicine 2007.
structures.note: Lower neck, top of the scapula and the shoulder region above the level of the scapular spine. Together with C2–3, one of the two most frequently implicated levels in chronic neck pain (~35% of cases).

structures.name: C6–C7 facet joint
structures.source: Dwyer, Aprill & Bogduk, Spine 1990 — volunteer distension; Fukui et al., Pain 1996.
structures.note: Extends caudally as far as the scapular spine. Fukui: superior scapular angle 48%, mid-scapular 41%, lower posterior cervical 33%.

structures.name: C7–T1 facet joint
structures.source: Fukui et al., Pain 1996 — intra-articular contrast/dorsal ramus stimulation in 61 SYMPTOMATIC patients. Not covered by the Dwyer volunteer study.
structures.note: Mid-scapular region in 86% of patients; superior angle of scapula in 28%. Note this level rests on patient-provocation data only — a tier below the C2–3 to C6–7 volunteer maps.

structures.name: Upper thoracic facet joints (T1–T4)
structures.source: Fukui et al., Reg Anesth 1997 (symptomatic patients, T1–2/T2–3); Dreyfuss, Tibiletti & Dreyer, Spine 1994 (volunteers, from T3–4 down).
structures.note: Local paraspinal pain lateral to the joint, from about half a segment above to a full segment below the joint of origin. Does not cross the midline and does not reliably distinguish adjacent levels.

structures.name: Mid thoracic facet joints (T5–T8)
structures.source: Dreyfuss, Tibiletti & Dreyer, Spine 1994 — distension in asymptomatic volunteers (T3–4 to T10–11).
structures.note: Local paraspinal zone lateral to the joint, half a segment above to one segment below. IMPORTANT: 27% of injected joints produced no pain at all, and the resulting patterns overlap heavily with costotransverse joint and soft-tissue patterns — thoracic maps are far less segment-discriminating than the cervical ones.

structures.name: Lower thoracic facet joints (T9–T12)
structures.source: Dreyfuss et al., Spine 1994 — volunteers, but only as far down as T10–11; Fukui et al., Reg Anesth 1997 — T11–12, symptomatic patients only.
structures.note: Paraspinal pain at and just below the segment, with modest lateral spread into the flank. Graded B rather than A because the range is split: T9–10 and T10–11 have volunteer-provocation evidence, but T11–12 rests on symptomatic-patient data alone. Same caveat as the rest of the thoracic spine: granular per-segment diagrams circulating in handouts are illustrative composites, not something either primary study reports.

structures.name: C2–C3 intervertebral disc
structures.source: Schellhas et al., AJNR 2000 — provocation discography, 40 chronic head/neck pain patients; Slipman et al., Spine J 2005 (41 subjects, 101 maps).
structures.note: Head pain is disproportionately a C2–3 phenomenon: 19/40 reported head pain (occipital most common, then temporal, then parietal) and 4 patients had EXCLUSIVELY head pain with no neck component. 80% of painful C2–3 discs looked normal on MRI.

structures.name: C3–C4 intervertebral disc
structures.source: Slipman et al., Spine J 2005 (19 maps); Grubb & Kelly, Spine 2000.
structures.note: Neck, subocciput, trapezius, anterior neck, face, shoulder, interscapular and limb — one of the broadest referral fields of any cervical disc.

structures.name: C4–C5 intervertebral disc
structures.source: Slipman et al., Spine J 2005 (27 maps); Grubb & Kelly, Spine 2000.
structures.note: Neck, shoulder, interscapular, trapezius, extremity, face, chest, subocciput. Grubb & Kelly found anterior chest wall referral begins at this level.

structures.name: C5–C6 intervertebral disc
structures.source: Slipman et al., Spine J 2005 (27 maps); Grubb & Kelly, Spine 2000.
structures.note: Neck, trapezius, interscapular, subocciput, anterior neck, chest, face. Bilateral pain occurred in 30–62% of discs at every level — laterality of pain does NOT indicate laterality of pathology.

structures.name: C6–C7 intervertebral disc
structures.source: Slipman et al., Spine J 2005 (16 maps); Grubb & Kelly, Spine 2000.
structures.note: Neck, interscapular, trapezius, shoulder, extremity, subocciput. Arm referral is most consistent at this level and C5–6.

structures.name: C7–T1 intervertebral disc
structures.source: Grubb & Kelly, Spine 2000; Slipman et al., Spine J 2005 (only 2 maps at this level).
structures.note: Mid-posterior neck through to the mid-thoracic spine, and the interscapular region. Very few mapped cases — the weakest-supported of the cervical disc levels.

structures.name: C4 nerve root (dynatome)
structures.source: Slipman et al., Spine 1998 — fluoroscopically guided cervical nerve root stimulation, 134 stimulations in 87 subjects (only 4 at C4).
structures.note: Base of neck and top of shoulder. Only 4 stimulations at this level — the least-supported root map.

structures.name: C5 nerve root (dynatome)
structures.source: Slipman et al., Spine 1998 (14 stimulations at C5).
structures.note: Lateral shoulder and lateral arm. NOTE: dynatomal (symptom) maps are measurably broader than textbook dermatomes — the expected pattern held in as little as 54% of stimulations.

structures.name: C6 nerve root (dynatome)
structures.source: Slipman et al., Spine 1998 (43 stimulations at C6).
structures.note: Lateral arm, dorsoradial forearm, thumb and index finger — but ~30% of C6 stimulations also produced LITTLE FINGER symptoms, classically a C8 finding. Intrathecal anastomoses between adjacent dorsal roots (up to ~61%) blur segment-specific territories.
structures.lookalikes: C7 root; radial tunnel; de Quervain's; carpal tunnel

structures.name: C7 nerve root (dynatome)
structures.source: Slipman et al., Spine 1998 (52 stimulations at C7 — the largest subgroup).
structures.note: Posterior arm, dorsal forearm, middle finger, and prominent interscapular/scapular referral. Proximal (scapular) referral is far more common in dynatomal maps than dermatome charts suggest.

structures.name: C8 nerve root (dynatome)
structures.source: Slipman et al., Spine 1998 (21 stimulations at C8).
structures.note: Ulnar forearm, ring and little fingers — but ~24% of C8 stimulations produced INDEX FINGER symptoms, classically a C6/C7 finding. Symptom location does not reliably localise the root.
structures.lookalikes: Cubital tunnel; Guyon's canal; neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome

structures.name: Cervical interspinous ligaments
structures.source: Kellgren, Clin Sci 1939 — hypertonic saline injection in volunteers; replicated in principle by Feinstein et al. 1954.
structures.note: Deep, diffuse, segmentally-organised ache in the neck and shoulder girdle that does NOT follow dermatomes. Foundational but small-N, non-blinded 1930s–50s work; Inman & Saunders noted the resulting maps 'could not be given with any great precision'.

structures.name: Thoracic interspinous ligaments
structures.source: Kellgren, Clin Sci 1939; Feinstein et al. 1954.
structures.note: Segmental paraspinal ache with lateral spread around the chest wall. Superficial structures (supraspinous ligament, spinous process) give sharply localised pain instead — the depth of the structure, not its level, determines whether pain refers.

structures.name: Acromioclavicular joint
structures.source: Gerber, Galantay & Hersche, JSES 1998 — hypertonic saline injection mapping in asymptomatic volunteers. (Sample size not verifiable from open sources.)
structures.note: Burning pain over the joint itself, deep in the supraspinatus fossa and upper trapezius, sometimes extending to the anterolateral deltoid and anterolateral neck. Can convincingly mimic cervical or trapezius myofascial pain.
structures.lookalikes: Upper trapezius myofascial pain; C4–5/C5–6 facet; cervical radiculopathy

structures.name: Subacromial space / bursa
structures.source: Gerber, Galantay & Hersche, JSES 1998 — hypertonic saline injection in asymptomatic volunteers.
structures.note: Intense pain at the lateral border of the acromion and over the lateral deltoid — a more focal and more distal pattern than AC joint referral. This is the classic 'impingement' distribution.
structures.lookalikes: C5 radiculopathy; supraspinatus/infraspinatus myofascial referral; axillary nerve entrapment

structures.name: Upper trapezius
structures.source: Zone map: Travell & Simons Vol. 1 (clinical observation). Referral DIRECTION separately corroborated by controlled hypertonic saline injection in healthy volunteers (Graven-Nielsen, Arendt-Nielsen et al.).
structures.note: Posterolateral neck up to the temple — the classic unilateral 'tension headache' pattern — and the angle of the jaw. Spillover to occiput and mastoid. One of only two muscles here whose referral DIRECTION has independent experimental support; the grade stays C because the mapped zone borders still come from clinical observation, and the saline work corroborates direction, not extent.
structures.lookalikes: C2–3 facet; cervicogenic headache; migraine

structures.name: Middle trapezius
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Superficial burning ache between the vertebral border of the scapula and the spine, locally over C7–T3.

structures.name: Lower trapezius
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Local ache at the T6–T9 paraspinal origin and over the top of the shoulder, with spillover to the base of the neck and mastoid — Travell & Simons specifically flag this 'far' referral as atypical.

structures.name: Levator scapulae
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Angle of the neck (the neck–shoulder junction) and along the vertebral border of the scapula to its inferior angle. Classically limits cervical rotation toward the painful side.

structures.name: Sternocleidomastoid (both heads)
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Sternal head: vertex, cheek/malar region, supraorbital ridge, deep in the ear, pharynx (sore-throat sensation), sternum. Clavicular head: bilateral frontal headache, deep ear pain, plus autonomic phenomena (postural dizziness, disequilibrium, tinnitus, lacrimation) that are a hallmark feature.
structures.lookalikes: Trigeminal neuralgia; TMD; cervicogenic dizziness; sinus headache

structures.name: Scalenes (anterior / middle / posterior)
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Anterior/pectoral chest wall, vertebral border of scapula, and down the radial forearm to thumb and index finger — closely mimics C6 radiculopathy. Posterior scalene skews more interscapular.
structures.lookalikes: C6 radiculopathy; neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome; carpal tunnel

structures.name: Splenius capitis
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: A 'boring' pain focused at the very top of the head. Classically no frontal or ocular involvement — that absence distinguishes it from sternocleidomastoid.

structures.name: Splenius cervicis
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Retro-orbital pain (behind the eye) and the angle of the neck/occiput, with reported ipsilateral blurred vision as a concomitant.

structures.name: Suboccipital group
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Diffuse, deep, band- or 'halo'-like pain from the occiput over the top of the head toward the temple and eye. Travell & Simons note this pattern does not map to a crisp cutaneous zone.

structures.name: Rhomboid major / minor
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Superficial, localised ache along the vertebral border of the scapula. One of the few patterns with essentially NO spillover and no projection into the arm — that confinement is the diagnostic clue.

structures.name: Supraspinatus
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Deep, boring ache centred over the mid-deltoid, spilling down the arm and forearm, occasionally to the wrist.
structures.lookalikes: Subacromial impingement; C5 radiculopathy

structures.name: Infraspinatus
structures.source: Zone map: Travell & Simons Vol. 1. Referral direction separately corroborated by hypertonic saline injection in healthy volunteers producing referred pain in the ipsilateral upper arm (Leffler et al., Eur J Pain 2000).
structures.note: Deep ache in the ANTERIOR shoulder/deltoid — the single most classic 'shoulder pain' myofascial pattern. Spillover down the lateral arm and radial forearm, plus local pain at the vertebral border of the scapula. Characteristically painful at rest and prevents sleeping on the affected side. The experimental corroboration covers only the arm component, not the anterior-deltoid, forearm or scapular zones, so the grade stays C with the rest of the myofascial maps.
structures.lookalikes: C5 radiculopathy (has weakness/reflex change); subacromial bursitis (painful arc); AC joint

structures.name: Teres minor
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: A small, circumscribed patch of deep ache over the posterior deltoid near the axillary scapular border. Notably does NOT radiate — the confinement is the clue.

structures.name: Teres major
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Posterior deltoid and the inferior angle of the scapula, spilling down the back of the arm toward the elbow.

structures.name: Subscapularis
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Severe deep pain over the posterior shoulder and scapula — the 'shoulder holster' pattern — with a distinctive circumferential band around the wrist in severe cases. Strongly associated with frozen-shoulder-type restriction.
structures.lookalikes: Adhesive capsulitis; posterior labral pathology

structures.name: Deltoid (anterior / posterior)
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Localised to the involved third of the muscle itself, spreading only into the adjacent upper arm. Unusual among shoulder muscles for NOT projecting distal to the elbow.

structures.name: Latissimus dorsi
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Constant ache over the inferior angle of the scapula and mid-back (the 'cape' of pain), spilling down the medial/posterior arm to the medial epicondyle and into the ring and little fingers.
structures.lookalikes: C8 radiculopathy; cubital tunnel

structures.name: Pectoralis major
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Anterior chest wall and breast. Clinically important: sternal-head trigger points near the 5th–6th costal cartilage can produce precordial pain and arrhythmia-like sensations that mimic cardiac disease — a well-documented diagnostic pitfall. Spillover down the medial arm to the ulnar digits.
structures.lookalikes: Angina / cardiac pain (EXCLUDE FIRST); costochondritis; C8–T1 radiculopathy

structures.name: Pectoralis minor
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Anterior chest and shoulder below the clavicle, referring down the medial arm and forearm to the ulnar three digits — overlapping the ulnar/thoracic outlet pattern.
structures.lookalikes: Neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome (subcoracoid space); C8 radiculopathy

structures.name: Serratus anterior
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Lateral chest wall in the mid-axillary line — the classic 'stitch in the side' — wrapping to the inferior scapular angle and down the medial arm to the ulnar forearm and digits. Often accompanied by air hunger / difficulty taking a deep breath.

structures.name: Serratus posterior superior
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Deep, poorly localised ache UNDER the scapula, referring down the posterior arm to the ulnar forearm, hand and little finger, with occasional numbness in a C8–T1 distribution. The 'ache I can't reach'.
structures.lookalikes: C8 radiculopathy; neurogenic thoracic outlet syndrome

structures.name: Coracobrachialis
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Anterior deltoid and front of the upper arm, with an unusually long reach for a small muscle — down the entire posterior arm to the dorsal forearm and hand.

structures.name: Biceps brachii
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Anterior shoulder (front of deltoid) and down the front of the arm to the antecubital crease.

structures.name: Triceps brachii
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1 (multiple distinct trigger point sites).
structures.note: Posterior shoulder, posterior upper arm and the olecranon/posterior elbow, spilling down the posterior forearm to the dorsum of the hand.

structures.name: Brachialis
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Front of the elbow over the muscle belly, with a distinctive projection to the base and dorsal web space of the THUMB — that thumb referral is the signature.
structures.lookalikes: C6 radiculopathy; de Quervain's; CMC arthritis

structures.name: Brachioradialis
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Lateral epicondyle ('tennis elbow' mimic) and down the dorsoradial forearm to the web space between thumb and index finger.
structures.lookalikes: Lateral epicondylalgia; radial tunnel syndrome; C6 radiculopathy

structures.name: Supinator
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Lateral epicondyle and proximal dorsal forearm — mimics resistant lateral epicondylalgia and radial tunnel syndrome — with spillover to the dorsal thumb web space.
structures.lookalikes: Lateral epicondylalgia (resistant); PIN/radial tunnel entrapment

structures.name: Pronator teres
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Volar proximal forearm and radial wrist, spilling to the radial three digits and thenar region. Can accompany true median nerve paresthesia (pronator teres syndrome).
structures.lookalikes: Carpal tunnel syndrome; pronator syndrome; C6 radiculopathy

structures.name: Wrist extensors (ECRL / ECRB / ECU)
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: ECRL/ECRB: lateral epicondyle spilling to the dorsum of the hand and wrist (ECRB into the dorsal middle finger). ECU stays fairly localised to the dorsal-ulnar wrist.
structures.lookalikes: Lateral epicondylalgia; C6–C7 radiculopathy

structures.name: Finger extensors (EDC / EIP)
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Dorsal forearm and wrist referring into the dorsum of the corresponding finger(s) — a roughly segmental, one-slip-per-finger pattern.

structures.name: Wrist / finger flexors (FCR, FCU, FDS, FDP)
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Volar forearm referring to the palm, volar wrist and corresponding fingers — FCU skews ulnar/little finger, FCR skews radial palm. Palmaris longus is distinct: a superficial, hypersensitive 'pins-and-needles' patch in the centre of the palm rather than a deep ache.
structures.lookalikes: Carpal tunnel syndrome; Guyon's canal; C8 radiculopathy

structures.name: Adductor pollicis
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Base of the thumb, thumb–index web space, centre of the palm and the wrist. Confined to the hand — can convincingly mimic carpal tunnel syndrome.
structures.lookalikes: Carpal tunnel syndrome; CMC arthritis

structures.name: Opponens pollicis
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Runs the length of the palmar/radial thumb itself, occasionally to the dorsal thumb and volar wrist.

structures.name: First dorsal interosseous
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Radial side of the index finger, running its full length to the fingertip, plus the dorsal web space. Frequently mistaken for digital nerve entrapment.
structures.lookalikes: Digital nerve entrapment; C6/C7 radiculopathy

structures.name: Rectus abdominis
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Hallmark feature: upper trigger points refer BILATERALLY across the mid and low back and can mimic epigastric or cardiac pain; lower trigger points refer bilaterally to the low back and sacral region and can produce colicky abdominal pain with GI symptoms.
structures.lookalikes: Visceral pathology (EXCLUDE FIRST); lumbar facet; discogenic low back pain

structures.name: External / internal obliques
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Upper fibres refer to the epigastrium and mimic heartburn; lower fibres refer to the groin and, in men, the testicle/scrotum. A well-known McBurney's-point mimic on the right — sometimes mistaken for appendicitis.
structures.lookalikes: Appendicitis (EXCLUDE FIRST); inguinal hernia; hip pathology

structures.name: Iliocostalis thoracis
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Segmental paraspinal band at the level of the trigger point that WRAPS AROUND THE CHEST WALL following the rib contours — can mimic cardiac or pleuritic pain.
structures.lookalikes: Cardiac / pleuritic pain (EXCLUDE FIRST); thoracic facet; costotransverse joint

structures.name: Iliocostalis lumborum
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Local low back extending into the buttock; sits more lateral than the longissimus pattern.

structures.name: Longissimus thoracis
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Paraspinal band at the trigger point level — upper points stay local with some radiation toward the scapula; lower points extend into the buttock, generally more MEDIAL than the iliocostalis lumborum pattern.

structures.name: Multifidi
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Very localised deep segmental pain directly over or adjacent to the spinous process at the level involved. Cervical level refers to the occiput; lumbosacral level refers to the buttock and occasionally the posterior thigh, mimicking sciatica.
structures.lookalikes: Lumbar radiculopathy; facet joint pain

structures.name: Serratus posterior inferior
structures.source: Travell & Simons Vol. 1.
structures.note: Localised, persistent ache at the thoracolumbar junction over the muscle itself. One of the more confined trunk patterns — in sharp contrast to serratus posterior superior's long reach into the hand.

structures.name: L1–L2 facet joint
structures.source: Mooney & Robertson, Clin Orthop 1976 (N=20, 5 volunteers + 15 patients); McCall, Park & O'Brien, Spine 1979 (asymptomatic volunteers); Fukui et al., Clin J Pain 1997 (symptomatic); Marks, Pain 1989.
structures.note: Upper lumbar facets refer laterally and proximally — flank, iliac crest and lateral hip — rather than down the leg. McCall's volunteer data put the upper levels in the flank and greater trochanter region.

structures.name: L2–L3 facet joint
structures.source: Mooney & Robertson, Clin Orthop 1976 (N=20, 5 volunteers + 15 patients); McCall, Park & O'Brien, Spine 1979 (asymptomatic volunteers); Fukui et al., Clin J Pain 1997 (symptomatic); Marks, Pain 1989.
structures.note: Lumbar paraspinal with lateral spread to the iliac crest and trochanter. Level-specific maps overlap heavily — McCall's own conclusion was 'considerable overlap' between levels.

structures.name: L3–L4 facet joint
structures.source: Mooney & Robertson, Clin Orthop 1976 (N=20, 5 volunteers + 15 patients); McCall, Park & O'Brien, Spine 1979 (asymptomatic volunteers); Fukui et al., Clin J Pain 1997 (symptomatic); Marks, Pain 1989.
structures.note: Lumbar paraspinal, iliac crest, upper buttock and greater trochanter, beginning to reach the lateral thigh.

structures.name: L4–L5 facet joint
structures.source: Mooney & Robertson, Clin Orthop 1976 (N=20, 5 volunteers + 15 patients); McCall, Park & O'Brien, Spine 1979 (asymptomatic volunteers); Fukui et al., Clin J Pain 1997 (symptomatic); Marks, Pain 1989.
structures.note: One of the two most commonly implicated levels. Buttock and trochanteric referral dominate; Marks (1989) attributed most buttock and trochanteric pain to L4–L5.

structures.name: L5–S1 facet joint
structures.source: Mooney & Robertson, Clin Orthop 1976 (N=20, 5 volunteers + 15 patients); McCall, Park & O'Brien, Spine 1979 (asymptomatic volunteers); Fukui et al., Clin J Pain 1997 (symptomatic); Marks, Pain 1989.
structures.note: Buttock and posterior thigh. Whether facet pain can reach below the knee is genuinely contested: Mooney & Robertson saw whole-leg pain in 3 of 20, but that is now widely attributed to large-volume saline rupturing the capsule. Windsor's electrical stimulation — a more specific stimulus — produced smaller, more proximal zones.
structures.lookalikes: SI joint (indistinguishable by pain location alone — DePalma 2011); L5/S1 radiculopathy

structures.name: L3–L4 intervertebral disc
structures.source: Vanharanta / Ohnmeiss provocation discography series; Carragee et al., Spine 2000 (false-positive rates); DePalma et al., PM&R 2011 (midline vs paramidline).
structures.note: Midline low back pain with anterior/lateral thigh referral. Discography localises the level poorly — overlap between adjacent levels is the norm.

structures.name: L4–L5 intervertebral disc
structures.source: Vanharanta / Ohnmeiss provocation discography series; Carragee et al., Spine 2000 (false-positive rates); DePalma et al., PM&R 2011 (midline vs paramidline).
structures.note: Midline low back pain, buttock and posterolateral leg. DePalma 2011: midline pain was present in 95.8% of confirmed discogenic cases versus 15.4% of facet and 12.9% of SI joint cases — the one location finding with real discriminating value.
structures.lookalikes: L5 radiculopathy; lumbar facet (but midline location favours disc)

structures.name: L5–S1 intervertebral disc
structures.source: Vanharanta / Ohnmeiss provocation discography series; Carragee et al., Spine 2000 (false-positive rates); DePalma et al., PM&R 2011 (midline vs paramidline).
structures.note: Midline low back, buttock, posterior thigh and calf. Pain extending below the knee correlates with the grade of annular disruption, not with which level is symptomatic.

structures.name: L3 nerve root
structures.source: Clinical radiculopathy series; ASIA sensory points; Suri et al. 2011 (femoral stretch test).
structures.note: Anterior and distal thigh to the medial knee. Prone knee bend is the loading test — 70% sensitive and 88% specific for L3 specifically.

structures.name: L4 nerve root
structures.source: Clinical radiculopathy series; ASIA sensory points.
structures.note: Medial leg and medial malleolus, with anterior thigh involvement. The transitional root — it feeds both the femoral nerve and the lumbosacral trunk, so it can present like an upper or a lower lumbar lesion.

structures.name: L5 nerve root
structures.source: Clinical radiculopathy series; ASIA sensory points; SLR/slump literature.
structures.note: Lateral leg, dorsum of foot, great toe and first web space, with buttock and posterolateral thigh referral proximally. The commonest lumbar radiculopathy alongside S1.
structures.lookalikes: Common fibular n. at the fibular neck (spares hip abduction and inversion); gluteus minimus TrP

structures.name: S1 nerve root
structures.source: Clinical radiculopathy series; ASIA sensory points.
structures.note: Posterior thigh and calf into the lateral foot and lateral malleolus. Achilles reflex loss is the localising sign.
structures.lookalikes: Piriformis / deep gluteal syndrome; SI joint; hamstring pathology

structures.name: Lumbar & sacral interspinous ligaments
structures.source: Kellgren, Clin Sci 1939; Feinstein et al., JBJS 1954 (as conventionally reported — the level-specific zones could not be verified against the primary tables).
structures.note: Deep, diffuse, segmentally-organised ache that does NOT follow dermatomes. Upper lumbar levels refer to flank and hip; lower lumbar and sacral levels refer into buttock and posterior thigh, approaching the knee in a minority. Foundational but small-N, non-blinded work.

structures.name: Sacroiliac joint
structures.source: Zone geometry: Fortin et al., Spine 1994 Part I — 10 ASYMPTOMATIC volunteers (grade-A design). All quoted percentages: Slipman et al., Arch Phys Med Rehabil 2000 — 50 SYMPTOMATIC patients (68 joints; 18 bilateral, 32 unilateral), selected by a single positive intra-articular block.
structures.note: Graded B, not A: only the zone SHAPE — a consistent 3 × 10 cm area immediately caudal to the PSIS — comes from asymptomatic volunteers. Every percentage below comes from a symptomatic patient series. Slipman: buttock 94%, lower lumbar 72%, lower extremity roughly a quarter to a half (secondary sources report 28% and 50% for the same dataset), groin 14%, upper lumbar 6%. So SI pain CAN go below the knee — 'it stays above the knee' is not a safe rule.
structures.lookalikes: L5–S1 facet (DePalma 2011: paramidline location cannot separate the two); lumbar disc

structures.name: Hip joint
structures.source: Lesher et al., Pain Medicine 2008 — fluoroscopically-guided intra-articular injection with pre-injection pain mapping, N=51 symptomatic patients.
structures.note: Buttock 71% — more common than groin, which contradicts the classic teaching. Thigh 57%, groin 55%, distal to knee 22%, foot 6%, isolated knee 2%, lower lumbar spine 0%. Fourteen distinct referral patterns were identified: there is no single dominant hip pattern.
structures.lookalikes: L2–L4 radiculopathy; SI joint; greater trochanteric pain syndrome. In adolescents with knee pain, always examine the hip — SCFE presents as knee pain in ~15%.

structures.name: Knee joint (intra-articular)
structures.source: Clinical observation; no controlled volunteer referral-mapping study identified.
structures.note: Largely local, with referral into the anterior thigh and proximal calf. Graded C because — unlike the hip and SI joint — no controlled provocation mapping study was found for the knee.

structures.name: Gluteus maximus
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Diffuse ache over the buttock mass. The medial-fibre trigger point near the coccyx mimics coccydynia. Rarely crosses the knee.
structures.lookalikes: Coccydynia; SI joint dysfunction

structures.name: Gluteus medius
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Posterior iliac crest, sacrum and the whole buttock — the classic 'low back pain' muscle. Spillover into the posterior thigh and upper calf.
structures.lookalikes: SI joint dysfunction; lumbar facet; L5 radiculopathy

structures.name: Gluteus minimus
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: THE pseudo-sciatica pattern, and the most convincing non-radicular mimic in the whole atlas. Anterior fibres refer from the lateral buttock down the OUTSIDE of the leg as far as the ankle; posterior fibres run down the back of the buttock and thigh, stopping at the calf. Leg pain to the ankle with no dermatomal, myotomal or reflex change should raise this immediately.
structures.lookalikes: L5 or S1 radiculopathy — the discriminator is the ABSENCE of reflex, myotome and dermatome findings

structures.name: Piriformis
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Over the SI joint, sacrum, buttock and posterior hip, extending into the proximal two-thirds of the posterior thigh. Distinguish the myofascial referral (rarely past the knee) from true piriformis syndrome — sciatic nerve entrapment — which does produce symptoms to the foot.
structures.lookalikes: Deep gluteal syndrome (true nerve entrapment); SI joint; S1 radiculopathy

structures.name: Tensor fasciae latae
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Anterolateral hip over the greater trochanter and down the lateral thigh along the IT band toward the lateral knee.
structures.lookalikes: Greater trochanteric pain syndrome; IT band syndrome

structures.name: Iliopsoas
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: A vertical band in the ipsilateral upper lumbar paraspinal region plus anterior groin, spilling into the anterior thigh to the knee. A frequently missed mimic of discogenic back pain.
structures.lookalikes: Discogenic low back pain; hip flexor strain; intra-articular hip pathology

structures.name: Quadratus lumborum
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Superficial layer refers along the iliac crest and into the lower buttock and greater trochanter; deep layer concentrates over the SI joint, with spillover to the groin and lower lateral abdomen. One of the most consistently missed sources of 'SI joint' pain.
structures.lookalikes: SI joint dysfunction; greater trochanteric pain syndrome; hip pathology

structures.name: Rectus abdominis (lower fibres)
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Refers as a band across the LOW BACK bilaterally, plus sacral and pelvic pain — easily missed because the examination focuses on posterior structures.
structures.lookalikes: Mechanical low back pain; visceral/gynaecological pathology (exclude first)

structures.name: Adductor longus / brevis
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Deep groin and anteromedial thigh, running down the medial leg to just below the knee.
structures.lookalikes: Adductor strain; osteitis pubis; hip labral pathology

structures.name: Adductor magnus
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Ischiocondylar portion refers along the posteromedial thigh to the knee; the proximal/pubic portion produces a deep intrapelvic ache that may be perceived intravaginally or intrarectally.
structures.lookalikes: Chronic pelvic pain syndromes; adductor strain

structures.name: Pectineus
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Sharply localised deep pain in the groin crease with minimal spillover.
structures.lookalikes: Hip labral tear; intra-articular hip pathology; femoroacetabular impingement

structures.name: Gracilis
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: A diffuse, superficial ache with an itching quality along the medial thigh — distinctively surface-level rather than deep, which separates it from adductor longus.

structures.name: Obturator internus
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Deep pelvic floor, coccyx and posterior vaginal or rectal wall, spilling into the perineum and posterior thigh.
structures.lookalikes: Pudendal neuralgia; levator ani syndrome

structures.name: Levator ani / coccygeus
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Coccyx and lower sacrum — the coccydynia pattern — with buttock referral and a sensation of rectal fullness.
structures.lookalikes: Coccydynia; levator ani syndrome; proctalgia fugax

structures.name: Rectus femoris
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Deep anterior thigh and, characteristically, the ANTERIOR KNEE — the referral is felt distally even though the trigger point sits proximally near the ASIS.
structures.lookalikes: Patellofemoral pain syndrome

structures.name: Vastus lateralis
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: The widest referral of the quadriceps group — the entire lateral thigh from hip to knee, with the most distal trigger point referring to the lateral knee and proximal ones to the lateral hip and buttock.
structures.lookalikes: IT band syndrome; lateral knee pain; greater trochanteric pain syndrome

structures.name: Vastus medialis
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Medial knee, with the superior (VMO) trigger point referring deep into the knee joint. Classically associated with a reflex-inhibition 'buckling' or giving-way sensation in the ABSENCE of true ligamentous laxity.
structures.lookalikes: Meniscal tear; ACL insufficiency (but ligament tests are negative); patellofemoral pain

structures.name: Vastus intermedius
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Diffuse, poorly localised mid-anterior thigh spreading toward the anterior knee. Often underappreciated in 'unexplained' anterior thigh ache.

structures.name: Sartorius
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Superficial, TINGLING or paraesthetic in quality — atypical for myofascial pain — running along the muscle from the anterolateral thigh toward the medial knee. The proximal trigger point near the ASIS can mimic meralgia paraesthetica.
structures.lookalikes: Meralgia paraesthetica (lateral femoral cutaneous n.)

structures.name: Biceps femoris
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Posterior thigh into the posterior knee and lateral popliteal fossa.
structures.lookalikes: Hamstring strain; S1 radiculopathy

structures.name: Semitendinosus / semimembranosus
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Lower buttock crease and posteromedial thigh down to the popliteal fossa — a distinct laterality from biceps femoris.
structures.lookalikes: Proximal hamstring tendinopathy; ischiogluteal bursitis

structures.name: Gastrocnemius
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Medial head refers to the medial calf and the instep/arch; lateral head to the posterior knee and lateral calf. Implicated in nocturnal calf cramps.
structures.lookalikes: DVT (EXCLUDE FIRST in an acutely swollen, warm calf); S1 radiculopathy

structures.name: Soleus
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: The LOWER trigger point near the Achilles refers to the HEEL and plantar surface — a textbook mimic of plantar fasciitis, reproducing weight-bearing heel pain. The upper/lateral trigger point refers, unexpectedly, to the SI JOINT region.
structures.lookalikes: Plantar fasciitis; Achilles tendinopathy; Baxter's neuropathy; SI joint dysfunction

structures.name: Popliteus
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Localised posterior knee pain, worse descending stairs or hills and with squatting. Minimal spillover.
structures.lookalikes: Popliteus tendinopathy; posterior horn meniscal tear; Baker's cyst

structures.name: Tibialis anterior
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Anterior ankle and the dorsum of the great toe and first ray, with local anterior shin pain.
structures.lookalikes: L5 radiculopathy; deep fibular n. entrapment; anterior compartment syndrome

structures.name: Tibialis posterior
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Diffuse — Achilles region, the ENTIRE plantar sole, and the posterior calf. The widest plantar distribution of any leg muscle.
structures.lookalikes: Tarsal tunnel syndrome; tibialis posterior tendinopathy; plantar fasciitis

structures.name: Fibularis (peroneus) longus / brevis
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Lateral malleolus and lateral ankle/foot; longus spills to the lateral foot dorsum, brevis to the lateral shin.
structures.lookalikes: Chronic lateral ankle instability; superficial fibular n. entrapment; L5/S1 radiculopathy

structures.name: Extensor digitorum longus
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Dorsum of the foot and anterolateral shin, referring into the dorsal aspect of the middle toes.

structures.name: Flexor digitorum longus
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Plantar surface over metatarsal heads 2–5, with a deep calf ache.

structures.name: Extensor digitorum brevis
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Local dorsolateral midfoot pain.

structures.name: Abductor hallucis
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Medial heel and medial plantar foot.
structures.lookalikes: Tarsal tunnel syndrome; medial-band plantar fasciitis

structures.name: Flexor digitorum brevis
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Plantar surface under metatarsal heads 2–4 and the central heel.

structures.name: Quadratus plantae
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Central plantar heel pad. Distinctively, it mimics plantar fasciitis WITHOUT arch involvement — that absence is the discriminator.
structures.lookalikes: Plantar fasciitis (but without arch pain); Baxter's neuropathy

structures.name: Foot interossei
structures.source: Travell & Simons, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction Vol. 2 (Lower Half of Body).
structures.note: Local pain in the corresponding toe and web space. Third and fourth web-space trigger points can mimic Morton's neuroma.
structures.lookalikes: Morton's neuroma; metatarsalgia; stress fracture

A.label: A — Experimental map, asymptomatic volunteers
A.desc: Referral zone produced by controlled provocation (intra-articular distension or injection) in asymptomatic volunteers, then charted. The strongest design available for referred-pain mapping: the zone is caused, not merely observed.

B.label: B — Provocation mapping in symptomatic patients
B.desc: Referral zone produced by provocation (discography, intra-articular stimulation, nerve root stimulation) in patients who already have pain. Real experimental data, but the population is sensitised and no asymptomatic control arm exists.

C.label: C — Clinical observation / expert synthesis
C.desc: Zone compiled from unblinded clinical case observation rather than controlled provocation. Useful for generating hypotheses; not validated diagnostic anatomy. Most myofascial referral maps sit here.
